home.meta_title: RAON Agent Factory — AI agents built for your business
home.meta_description: We connect your existing systems and business rules so recurring development, analysis, and operations work runs as AI agent workflows that are executed, verified, and operated.
home.title: AI agents built for your business — from build to execution, verification, and operation.
home.lede: We connect your existing systems and business rules to turn recurring development, analysis, and operations work into real execution flows.
home.concept: A factory that builds AI agents and puts them to real work.
home.cta_primary: Talk to us about an AI agent
home.flow_run_copy: Work runs one request at a time
home.flow_verify_copy: Checked with automated and on-screen checks
home.problem_title: Why AI experiments rarely become real work
home.problem_lede: Chat-style AI gives answers, but work is only done when it runs within the right permissions and the result is confirmed.
home.problem_access_title: It can't reach your systems or permissions
home.problem_access_copy: AI that isn't connected to real data and tools stops at suggestions, and people end up copying the results by hand.
home.problem_verify_title: There's no standard for checking results
home.problem_verify_copy: Without separating what is done from what is unverified, results are hard to put into operation.
home.problem_operate_copy: Without request, execution, and result records, the same problems get solved again and improvements are hard to find.
home.services_title: Start with one task and carry it through to operation
home.services_lede: We don't start with a large system. We define a workable scope and expand based on verified results.
home.service_pilot_copy: We pick one recurring task, build an agent workflow connected to your real systems, and review the results with you.
home.service_pilot_item3: Report of results and unverified items
home.service_build_copy: We turn the proven workflow into an agent that your users can send requests to and receive results from, fitted to your systems and rules.
home.service_build_item1: Integration with existing web and business systems
home.service_operate_copy: We use the requests and execution records gathered in operation to find failure points and keep improving the agent.
home.cases_title: Products we built and verified ourselves
home.cases_lede: These are not customer deliveries. They are our own products, built and verified in-house, with what was confirmed and what was not listed separately.
home.case_stock_summary: A mobile paper-trading product built by several AI development providers splitting implementation and verification request by request.
home.case_stock_problem: When several AI development tools build one product together, it easily becomes unclear who changed what and what has been confirmed.
home.case_stock_scope: Mobile paper-trading screens and product features were split into requests, implemented and revised by several providers, with the verification result of each request recorded.
home.case_stock_flow: Users trade with virtual funds on the paper-trading screens. On the development side, changes land in the order: request intake → provider implementation → verification → integration.
home.case_stock_verified: Development proceeded in our own environment while confirming the implementation and verification result of each request.
home.case_stock_unverified: Real brokerage integration, investment performance, and operation for external customers are outside this case and were not verified.
home.case_stock_fit: Teams using several AI development tools together can consider this approach to keep requests, implementation, and verification records in one flow.
home.case_hub_summary: On top of the open-source GNUBOARD7 (G7) 7.0.11, we added product screens and an AI workspace as extension modules without modifying the core.
home.case_hub_problem: Adding AI to a web service that is already running means adding new flows without breaking existing members, permissions, and screens.
home.case_hub_scope: Members, boards, search, and permissions come from G7 as-is. We added the product home and brand screens (raonslab-product) and an AI workspace for approved users (raonslab-ai-workspace) as extension modules.
home.case_hub_flow: Visitors keep using the community as before. Approved users send requests in the AI workspace, follow progress and results, and send follow-up instructions on the same request.
home.case_hub_verified: Native G7 checks J1–J10 PASS · AI adapter checks A1–A10 PASS · Mobile screens at 360/390/412px PASS · Same-request follow-up PASS · 0 core patches
home.case_hub_unverified: Commercial-scale traffic, long-term operational stability, and operation in external customer environments have not been verified yet.
home.case_hub_fit: Applicable when you want to add AI request, progress, and result flows to an existing web service as extensions, without changing its core.
home.process_title: Confirm small, then expand as far as it's confirmed
home.process_step1_copy: We hear about your recurring work and current systems, and choose one task to pilot first.
home.process_step2_copy: We agree in writing on the systems, data, permission boundaries, and success criteria the agent will work with.
home.process_step3_copy: We build an execution flow that actually runs within the agreed scope.
home.process_step4_copy: We share automated and on-screen check results, split into PASS, FAIL, and not verified.
home.process_step5_copy: We bring the verified flow into your work and keep improving it from operational records.
home.tech_title: Not a general chat, but an execution flow you can observe and verify
home.tech_lede: We design every agent so that what it was asked, what it executed, and how it was checked all remain on record.
home.tech_connect_copy: We use your systems' public APIs and extension points first and keep changes to core code to a minimum.
home.tech_permission_copy: Public pages, signed-in users, approved users, and administrators have separate permissions, and agent execution opens only within approved scope.
home.tech_observe_copy: Requests, progress events, results, and follow-up instructions stay in the same request record so the flow can always be traced.
home.tech_verify_copy: Only changes that pass automated checks and real browser and mobile screen checks go into the operating flow.
home.tech_report_copy: We report what was confirmed, what failed, and what has not been checked yet, without exaggeration.

services.title: Services
services.lede: We start by making one task actually run, then extend into a build and ongoing operation only as far as results are verified. For each service we list who it is for, what you receive, and what we do not promise.
services.overview_copy: The three services run in order. Verified results from one stage define the scope of the next.
services.flow1_copy: One task · success criteria · access boundary
services.pilot_copy: We pick one recurring task, build an agent run connected to your real system, and review the results together.
services.pilot_target1: Teams with recurring work but no clear starting point for AI
services.pilot_target2: Organizations that want to see it work before a larger commitment
services.pilot_output1: A definition of the target task and success criteria
services.pilot_output2: An agreed connection scope and access boundary
services.pilot_output3: One working run inside the agreed scope
services.pilot_output4: A results report split into pass, fail and not verified
services.pilot_limit1: It is a pilot of one task, not a full system build.
services.pilot_limit2: We do not promise impact or performance figures.
services.build_copy: We turn a verified run into an agent your users can request work from and receive results, fitted to your systems and rules.
services.build_target1: Organizations extending a finished pilot to real users
services.build_target2: Teams adding capability while keeping existing web or business systems
services.build_output1: Integration that prefers public APIs and extension points
services.build_output2: Screens for requests, progress and results
services.build_output3: Records of automated checks and real-screen checks
services.build_limit1: We do not guarantee integration with every system. If there is no way to connect, scope is renegotiated.
services.build_limit2: Changes that fail verification are not released.
services.operate_copy: Using requests and run records from operation, we find failure points, apply changed rules, and verify again.
services.operate_target1: Organizations running a built agent whose rules change often
services.operate_limit1: We do not currently offer an SLA, zero-downtime operation or long-term stability guarantees.

services.evidence1: Service definitions match the “Services” section of the home page.
services.evidence2: Unpublished values follow our rule of not publishing figures without an approved basis.

principles.title: Engineering principles
principles.lede: This page explains, from your side of the table, where an agent connects, who can do what, how results are checked, and what is recorded during operation. Internal tool names are listed separately at the bottom.
principles.api_copy: We use the public APIs and extension points your system already offers. Changes to core code are kept to a minimum; if unavoidable, the reason and scope are agreed first.
principles.api_example: On this site: product pages and the workspace were added purely as extension modules, without modifying the open-source CMS core.
principles.access_copy: Visibility and execution rights are split into levels. This site behaves as follows.
principles.level_public_copy: Business pages, reading notices, Q&A and community, search
principles.level_member_copy: Community participation per board permissions. No AI execution rights.
principles.level_approved_copy: Only separately approved accounts can send requests in the AI workspace and see their own results.
principles.level_admin_copy: Viewing and handling consultations (notes, status) are granted separately. The server enforces the final check.
principles.verify_copy: We combine automated tests with checks in a real browser, at phone widths of 360, 390 and 412px plus desktop, looking at overflow, focus and touch target size.
principles.verify_pass_copy: Confirmed by tests and on real screens
principles.operate_copy: Requests, progress, results and follow-ups are kept on the same request record. Before each release a restorable backup is made and its location is written into the release record.
principles.operate_report: We report what was confirmed, what failed and what was not checked — and never present unchecked items as confirmed.
principles.internal_copy: These are the internal components that implement the principles above on this site. This does not mean the same tools are installed in your environment.
principles.internal_g7: GNUBOARD7 7.0.11 — the open-source CMS this site runs on
principles.internal_product: raonslab-product — extension module for business pages and the consultation flow
principles.internal_ai: raonslab-ai-workspace — extension module for the approved-user AI workspace
principles.internal_agentopt: AI_GCS · AgentOpt — internal tools managing request-level development and verification (AI integration expansion currently on hold)
principles.evidence1: Access levels and the split consultation permissions are based on the route and permission settings of the product and AI workspace modules.
principles.evidence2: Verification widths and the backup step come from the product module’s release validation records.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.lede: This is not a final privacy policy. It separates how this site actually behaves today from the items that must be approved before launch.
privacy.draft_copy: Contact person, contact details, address, retention period and business details are not approved yet, so they are not filled in. This page will be updated once they are.
privacy.now1_copy: Currently closed. The consultation screen shows no personal-data fields and collects nothing.
privacy.now2_copy: Sign-up and sign-in are handled by the base CMS member feature. The account is for community use.
privacy.now3_copy: Notices, Q&A and community posts are public. Please do not put personal or confidential information in posts.
privacy.safe1: Consultation data is designed to be stored encrypted in a dedicated store.
privacy.safe2: Viewing and handling consultations are granted to administrators separately.
privacy.safe3: Consultation data is never forwarded automatically to boards, search, general notifications or AI requests.
privacy.safe4: Public responses never contain consultation personal data, and submissions from other sites are rejected.
privacy.launch_copy: Online intake stays closed until every condition below is approved and verified.
privacy.launch1: Production domain and HTTPS in place
privacy.launch2: Approved wording, policy and retention period
privacy.launch3: Encryption keys, backup, recovery and access control reviewed
privacy.launch4: Store/read/delete/restore drill without real customer data
privacy.evidence1: Current handling and safeguards are based on the consultation feature’s actual configuration (intake disabled) and implementation.
privacy.evidence2: Launch conditions come from the product module’s pre-launch checklist.

community.title: Service & community rules
community.lede: These are the rules we ask you to follow while using this site. Formal terms of service are not approved yet; until then this document sets our operating rules.
community.account1: Sign-up creates an account for using the community.
community.account2: AI workspace access is separate from sign-up and is granted only after separate approval.
community.account3: You do not need to sign in to request a consultation.
community.board_questions: Q&A — questions about the service and the site.
community.board_public: Posts are public. Personal data needed for a consultation is taken only through the consultation process, never via boards.
community.prohibited1: Posting your own or others’ personal data, account details or passwords
community.prohibited2: Sharing system details, access credentials or confidential material without authority
community.prohibited4: Unlawful content or content infringing others’ rights
community.pending2: Criteria and process for removing posts or restricting use
community.evidence1: The account/consultation relationship matches the consultation note on the home page.
community.evidence2: The board list reflects the current Notices, Q&A and Community board addresses.

ai_policy.title: AI workspace access, data & execution policy
ai_policy.lede: Signing up and being approved to run AI are different steps. This page explains who can enter the workspace, what is recorded, and what is never executed.
ai_policy.hold_title: AI integration expansion is on hold
ai_policy.hold_copy: We are focusing on the business pages and not expanding AI features for now. This page describes the access boundary as designed; it does not mean anyone can run AI.
ai_policy.access1: Entering the workspace needs both a signed-in account and workspace permission.
ai_policy.access2: Signed-out visitors are sent to sign-in; without permission the server rejects the request.
ai_policy.data1: Request number, status, title and the requesting account’s identifier are recorded so you only see your own requests.
ai_policy.data2: Credentials for external services are never sent to the browser.
ai_policy.data3: Consultation personal data is never forwarded to AI requests automatically.
ai_policy.exec1: Execution opens only for approved accounts within approved scope.
ai_policy.exec2: The screen never invents progress or completion times the server did not report.
ai_policy.exec3: Internal execution commands and raw events are not shown on regular screens.
ai_policy.pending1: How to apply for workspace access and approval criteria
ai_policy.pending3: Disclosure of any external AI processors
ai_policy.evidence1: Access conditions come from the AI workspace module’s sign-in/permission settings and an observed redirect to sign-in.
ai_policy.evidence2: Data and execution items come from the AI workspace module’s development rules and request record structure.
